primitives.name: Rule Shift Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: Indeed, the very fact that under the old rules it was possible to use a prearranged succession of plays without any signal except that of starting shows how radically the game has changed and how diametrically the disadvantage has been shifted from the defense to the attack.
primitives.assumptions: Defensive information advantage existed under old rules; this advantage is neutralized by mandatory signaling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Duality between defensive and offensive information asymmetry collapses at the point where signaling becomes obligatory.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state-transition logic where rule changes induce strategic pivot points, requiring adaptive state machines.
layer2.telemetry: Analysis of play sequence predictability before and after rule enforcement.

primitives.name: Two-Move Series Play
primitives.verbatim_quote: A series of more than two plays is hardly conceivable under present rules, but as an occasional surprise device I think the two-move series play may justly claim a place in modern tactics.
primitives.assumptions: The two-play sequence is the maximum viable unit given current signaling constraints and defensive read time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Three-play series become computationally intractable due to exponential increase in signaling overhead and defensive counter-strategy.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GSI optimal stopping theory for offensive drive termination, balancing risk vs. reward.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of two-play versus longer drive sequences.

The transition from "every man in every play" to mandatory signaling introduces a fundamental information-theoretic bottleneck. Under old rules, the offense could exploit pre-arranged deterministic sequences, treating each player as a fixed component in a static graph. The rule shift duality transforms the game into a dynamic Bayesian network where each signal updates posterior probabilities over defensive alignments. The two-move series play operates as a minimal sufficient statistic: it maximizes the entropy of the offensive action distribution while remaining within the Shannon capacity limit imposed by the signaling channel's bandwidth. This primitive also reveals a critical failure mode—when defensive players learn the statistical structure of these short series, the mutual information between offense and defense spikes, leading to catastrophic drive termination.
